words.enDefinition: People classified as either employed or unemployed under the survey's definitions

examples.en: The survey's labor force includes both people with jobs and people classified as unemployed.
examples.zh: 调查中的「劳动力人口」既包括有工作的人，也包括归类为失业的人。

examples.en: If more residents start looking for work, the measured labor force may grow.
examples.zh: 如果更多居民开始找工作，统计中的「劳动力人口」可能会增加。

words.enDefinition: US survey population of noninstitutionalized civilians aged sixteen or older

examples.en: The US survey table shows the civilian noninstitutional population separately from the number of workers.
examples.zh: 这份美国调查表分别列出「非机构平民人口」和劳动者人数。

examples.en: We divided employment by the civilian noninstitutional population to reproduce the US survey's ratio.
examples.zh: 我们用就业人数除以「非机构平民人口」，算出了这项美国调查的比率。

collocations: share of the civilian noninstitutional population
growth in the civilian noninstitutional population

words.enDefinition: Population falling within the age range used for a labor statistic

examples.en: The report defines the age range before comparing each country's working-age population.
examples.zh: 报告先说明年龄范围，再比较各国的「劳动年龄人口」。

examples.en: Our exercise uses the working-age population as the base for the participation measure.
examples.zh: 我们的习题用「劳动年龄人口」作为计算参与率的基数。

words.enDefinition: Share of the reference population that is employed or officially unemployed

examples.en: Our chart shows the labor force participation rate rising even though employment barely changed.
examples.zh: 我们的图表显示，尽管就业人数几乎没有变化，「劳动力参与率」仍有所上升。

examples.en: We used the survey's population count to calculate the labor force participation rate for that year.
examples.zh: 我们用该调查的人口统计值计算当年的「劳动力参与率」。

collocations: calculate the labor force participation rate
labor force participation rate by age

words.enDefinition: Share of the reference population counted as employed in the survey

examples.en: The employment-to-population ratio fell when employment grew more slowly than the population used for comparison.
examples.zh: 当就业人数的增长慢于参照人口时，「就业人口比」下降了。

examples.en: The class compared the employment-to-population ratio for adults in two different age brackets.
examples.zh: 全班比较了两个年龄组成年人的「就业人口比」。

words.enDefinition: Share of the labor force officially counted as unemployed under the definition

examples.en: We divided the number of unemployed workers by the labor force to calculate the unemployment rate.
examples.zh: 我们用失业人数除以劳动力人口，算出了「失业率」。

examples.en: A fall in the unemployment rate can occur when some jobseekers leave the labor force.
examples.zh: 部分求职者退出劳动力人口时，「失业率」可能下降。

words.enDefinition: Counted as neither employed nor unemployed under the survey's criteria

examples.en: The US survey lists retirees with no job or job search as not in the labor force.
examples.zh: 美国调查将没有工作也没在找工作的退休人员归为「不在劳动力人口中」。

examples.en: She was not in the labor force while studying full time and taking a break from job searches.
examples.zh: 她全日制就读并暂停求职期间，「不在劳动力人口中」。

collocations: classified as not in the labor force
people not in the labor force
counted as not in the labor force

words.enDefinition: Concrete actions taken recently to seek work under a survey's rules

examples.en: Contacting an employer directly counted as an active job search in the US example.
examples.zh: 在美国的示例中，直接联系雇主算作「积极求职」。

examples.en: Reading listings alone did not qualify as an active job search in this survey.
examples.zh: 在这项调查中，仅浏览招聘信息不算「积极求职」。

words.enDefinition: in the US CPS, people outside the labour force who want and are available for work and searched within the past year but outside the recent four-week window

examples.en: The US table lists marginally attached workers separately because they have not searched recently.
examples.zh: 美国统计表单列「边缘劳动力」，因为这些人近期没有寻找工作。

examples.en: In the US example, marginally attached workers searched sometime in the past year and still wanted work.
examples.zh: 在美国示例中，「边缘劳动力」过去一年内曾经求职，现在仍想工作。

words.zhGloss: 因前景不佳而放弃求职者
words.enDefinition: US marginally attached people not currently searching because of poor job prospects
acceptedZhAnswers: 因前景不佳而放弃求职者

examples.en: The survey counted some respondents as discouraged workers after they stopped expecting suitable openings.
examples.zh: 调查将一些不再相信会有合适岗位的受访者归为「因前景不佳而放弃求职者」。

examples.en: Under the US definition, discouraged workers are outside the labor force unless they resume searching.
examples.zh: 按美国的定义，「因前景不佳而放弃求职者」在恢复求职前不计入劳动力人口。

collocations: discouraged workers outside the labor force

words.enDefinition: US category for workers involuntarily working fewer than full-time hours for economic reasons

examples.en: Workers unable to find full-time work may be classified as working part time for economic reasons.
examples.zh: 无法找到全职工作的人，可能被归为「因经济原因兼职」。

examples.en: The US release reports workers employed part time for economic reasons alongside other measures of labor underutilization.
examples.zh: 美国这份报告把「因经济原因兼职」的人数和其他劳动力利用不足指标一同列出。

collocations: working part time for economic reasons
employed part time for economic reasons
counted as part time for economic reasons

words.enDefinition: Employment making less use of available hours or skills than workers want

examples.en: We discussed underemployment when workers wanted more hours than shops were offering.
examples.zh: 当劳动者希望工作更长时间但店家给不出更多工时时，我们讨论了「就业不足」。

examples.en: Our seminar compared underemployment among graduates working in jobs with different skill requirements.
examples.zh: 研讨课比较了岗位技能要求不同的毕业生所面临的「就业不足」。

words.enDefinition: Unused labor capacity including unemployment and some forms of insufficient employment

examples.en: The class compared two measures of labor underutilization from the same employment report.
examples.zh: 全班比较了同一份就业报告中的两项「劳动力利用不足」指标。

examples.en: Our exhibit uses labor underutilization to include both joblessness and some unmet demand for hours.
examples.zh: 我们的展示用「劳动力利用不足」来涵盖失业和部分未获满足的工时需求。

words.zhGloss: 美国扩展失业指标 U-5
words.enDefinition: the US BLS measure adding all marginally attached people to both total unemployment in the numerator and the civilian labour force in the denominator
acceptedZhAnswers: 美国扩展失业指标 U-5

examples.en: The report compared U-5 with unemployment after including people marginally attached to the labour force in its calculation.
examples.zh: 报告把边缘劳动力纳入计算之后，将「美国扩展失业指标 U-5」与通常的失业率作了比较。

examples.en: Our tutor used U-5 to show how including a group outside the labour force changed the reported rate.
examples.zh: 导师用「美国扩展失业指标 U-5」演示将劳动力之外的一类人口纳入计算如何改变所报比率。

words.enDefinition: the US BLS measure dividing unemployment, marginal attachment and part-time employment for economic reasons by the civilian labour force plus marginal attachment

examples.en: Our worksheet uses U-6 to include workers who want full-time jobs but work part time.
examples.zh: 我们的习题用了「美国广义失业率」，把想做全职工作却只能兼职的人也计入其中。

examples.en: The denominator of U-6 includes the civilian labor force and the marginally attached.
examples.zh: 「美国广义失业率」的分母包括平民劳动力人口和边缘劳动力。

words.enDefinition: Survey asking individuals or households about employment and other personal characteristics

examples.en: The US household survey counts an employed person once even if they hold two jobs.
examples.zh: 美国的「住户调查」中，即使同一个人有两份工作，也只计为一名就业者。

examples.en: We checked the household survey for information about people actively looking for work.
examples.zh: 我们在「住户调查」中查找积极求职者的相关数据。

words.enDefinition: Survey asking workplaces about payroll jobs, earnings, or employee hours

examples.en: In the US establishment survey, two covered payroll jobs held by one worker are counted separately.
examples.zh: 在美国的「用人单位调查」中，同一名劳动者的两个有薪岗位分别计数。

examples.en: We used the establishment survey to compare payroll jobs at factories and retail stores.
examples.zh: 我们用「用人单位调查」比较工厂和零售门店的有薪岗位。

words.enDefinition: US count of covered paid jobs at nonfarm establishments

examples.en: The class compared nonfarm payroll employment with the number of employed people from the household survey.
examples.zh: 全班比较了「非农就业岗位数」和住户调查中的就业人数。

examples.en: Our practice report showed nonfarm payroll employment holding steady even as manufacturing jobs declined.
examples.zh: 练习报告显示，尽管制造业岗位减少，「非农就业岗位数」总体持平。

words.enDefinition: US ratio of job openings to employment plus job openings

examples.en: Our US labor report places the job openings rate above the chart of actual hiring.
examples.zh: 我们的美国劳动力报告将「职位空缺率」放在实际招聘人数图表的上方。

examples.en: We reproduced the job openings rate using both occupied jobs and open positions in the denominator.
examples.zh: 我们将已有人任职的岗位和空缺岗位都纳入分母，重算出了「职位空缺率」。

words.enDefinition: US voluntary separations relative to employment, excluding retirements and transfers

examples.en: The quits rate fell in our example even though the number of layoffs rose.
examples.zh: 在我们的例子中，尽管裁员人数增加，「主动离职率」仍然下降。

examples.en: We used the quits rate to compare voluntary departures across sectors of different sizes.
examples.zh: 我们用「主动离职率」比较规模不同的行业中主动离职的情况。

words.enDefinition: Employer-initiated job separations grouped together in US labor turnover reports

examples.en: The US table reports layoffs and discharges separately from people who resign on their own.
examples.zh: 美国统计表将「裁员和解雇」与自愿辞职分开列报。

examples.en: Our group compared layoffs and discharges in manufacturing and retail using the same monthly release.
examples.zh: 我们小组用同一份月报比较了制造业和零售业的「裁员和解雇」数据。

words.enDefinition: Movement of workers into and out of positions over a period

examples.en: The labor turnover figures showed frequent hiring and departures despite little net employment change.
examples.zh: 「人员流动」数据显示，尽管净就业变化很小，招聘和离职都很频繁。

examples.en: We compared labor turnover across industries while holding the reporting period constant.
examples.zh: 我们使用同一统计期，比较各行业的「人员流动」。

words.enDefinition: Length of the current spell spent without work and classified unemployed

examples.en: The unemployment duration column records how long respondents have been in their current spell.
examples.zh: 「失业持续时间」一栏记录受访者本次失业持续多久。

examples.en: We compared median unemployment duration across respondents with different levels of education.
examples.zh: 我们比较了不同教育程度受访者的「失业持续时间」中位数。

words.enDefinition: Unemployment lasting at least the duration specified in the reporting framework

examples.en: The US long-term unemployment series groups people who have been unemployed for at least twenty-seven weeks.
examples.zh: 美国「长期失业」数据把已失业至少二十七周的人归为一类。

examples.en: Our class compared two reports that used different thresholds for long-term unemployment.
examples.zh: 全班比较了两份采用不同「长期失业」判定门槛的报告。

words.enDefinition: Unemployment while workers and employers take time to find suitable matches

examples.en: The model shows frictional unemployment while graduates look for openings that match their training.
examples.zh: 模型展示了毕业生寻找与培训经历匹配的岗位时发生的「摩擦性失业」。

examples.en: We discussed how a better job board could shorten spells of frictional unemployment.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了更好的招聘信息平台如何缩短「摩擦性失业」的持续时间。

words.enDefinition: Unemployment linked to a mismatch between workers and available jobs

examples.en: The exercise illustrates structural unemployment when vacancies require qualifications that local jobseekers lack.
examples.zh: 习题用空缺岗位要求本地求职者不具备的资质，说明「结构性失业」。

examples.en: Our group compared structural unemployment caused by a geographic mismatch with temporary search delays.
examples.zh: 小组比较了地域错配造成的「结构性失业」与暂时的求职延迟。

words.enDefinition: Unemployment associated with weak economic activity during a downturn

examples.en: The model shows cyclical unemployment among restaurant workers who lose jobs after overall spending falls.
examples.zh: 模型显示，总体支出下降后失去工作的餐饮业劳动者属于「周期性失业」。

examples.en: We separated cyclical unemployment from the unemployment that would remain after demand recovered.
examples.zh: 我们将「周期性失业」与需求恢复后仍会存在的失业分开。

words.enDefinition: Joblessness linked to recurring changes in labor demand during the year

examples.en: The town's seasonal unemployment rises after the summer visitors leave and hotels reduce staffing.
examples.zh: 夏季游客离开、酒店缩减用工后，小镇的「季节性失业」上升了。

examples.en: We discussed seasonal unemployment before comparing tourism employment from January and July.
examples.zh: 比较一月和七月的旅游业就业情况之前，我们讨论了「季节性失业」。

words.enDefinition: Process linking workers seeking jobs with employers offering suitable openings

examples.en: The model treats job matching as a process that can take several weeks.
examples.zh: 模型把「岗位匹配」看作一个可能需要几周的过程。

examples.en: Better information may improve job matching in a town with many unfilled vacancies.
examples.zh: 在空缺岗位很多的小镇，更充分的信息可能改善「岗位匹配」。

words.enDefinition: Share of unemployed people moving into employment during a specified period

examples.en: The quarterly job-finding rate rose when more unemployed respondents reported starting a job.
examples.zh: 随着更多失业受访者报告已入职，季度「求职成功率」上升了。

examples.en: The exercise calculates the job-finding rate among those unemployed at the start of June.
examples.zh: 习题计算的是六月初处于失业状态的人群的「求职成功率」。

words.enDefinition: Frequency of workers leaving existing employment relative to a defined workforce

examples.en: Our model raised the job separation rate while keeping the rate of successful job searches fixed.
examples.zh: 我们的模型在求职成功率不变的情况下提高了「离职率」。

examples.en: The instructor calculated the job separation rate from the number who left and the employment base.
examples.zh: 老师用离职人数和就业人数基数算出了「离职率」。

words.enDefinition: Graph relating job vacancies to unemployment across labor market conditions

examples.en: The tutor plotted a Beveridge curve with unemployment on one axis and vacancies on the other.
examples.zh: 老师画了「贝弗里奇曲线」，两条轴分别表示失业和空缺岗位。

examples.en: The outward shift in the Beveridge curve suggested weaker matching in our classroom model.
examples.zh: 在课堂模型中，「贝弗里奇曲线」外移说明匹配效率变低了。

words.enDefinition: Extent to which vacancies are plentiful relative to available jobseekers

examples.en: We measured labor market tightness using the number of vacancies for each unemployed person.
examples.zh: 我们用每名失业者对应的岗位空缺数衡量「劳动力市场紧俏度」。

examples.en: Our chart shows greater labor market tightness during the months when vacancies rose and unemployment fell.
examples.zh: 我们的图表显示，在岗位空缺增加、失业减少的几个月，「劳动力市场紧俏度」更高。

words.enDefinition: Available labor capacity that current employment and hours do not use

examples.en: We looked for labor market slack among both unemployed people and workers wanting more hours.
examples.zh: 我们从失业者和想获得更多工时的劳动者中寻找「劳动力市场闲置」的迹象。

examples.en: The report pairs lower vacancies with other signs of labor market slack in the example.
examples.zh: 该报告在示例中列出空缺岗位减少及其他「劳动力市场闲置」的迹象。

words.enDefinition: Percentage change in a broad measure of prices over a period

examples.en: We calculated the inflation rate from the change in the index over twelve months.
examples.zh: 我们根据十二个月内指数的变化计算了「通胀率」。

examples.en: A lower positive inflation rate still means the index rose during the comparison period.
examples.zh: 「通胀率」虽然下降但仍为正，说明指数在对比期间依旧上涨。

words.enDefinition: Measure of changes over time in prices paid for a consumer basket

examples.en: We used the consumer price index to compare consumer prices across several years in our worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们用「消费者价格指数」比较了习题中几年的消费价格。

examples.en: The consumer price index in the report summarizes changes across many categories of household spending.
examples.zh: 报告中的「消费者价格指数」汇总了家庭各类支出所对应的价格变化。

words.enDefinition: Measure of price changes received by domestic producers in the US framework

examples.en: The US producer price index tracks what sellers receive for their output in the example.
examples.zh: 在这个例子中，美国「生产者价格指数」追踪卖家出售产品所得的价格。

examples.en: We compared the producer price index with a consumer series covering a different spending basket.
examples.zh: 我们把「生产者价格指数」和覆盖不同消费篮子的消费者数据作了比较。

collocations: changes in the producer price index

words.zhGloss: 个人消费支出价格指数
words.enDefinition: US measure of prices for goods and services consumed by households
acceptedZhAnswers: 个人消费支出价格指数

examples.en: The US PCE price index includes certain purchases made on behalf of households, such as medical services.
examples.zh: 美国「个人消费支出价格指数」包含某些由他人为家庭支付的项目，例如医疗服务。

examples.en: The lecture compared the PCE price index with a consumer index that used different spending weights.
examples.zh: 课堂比较了「个人消费支出价格指数」与另一种采用不同支出权重的消费价格指数。

collocations: annual change in the PCE price index

words.enDefinition: Consumer price index compiled using shared methods for comparable European statistics

examples.en: We used the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices to compare inflation across two European countries in our assignment.
examples.zh: 作业中，我们用「调和消费者价格指数」比较了两个欧洲国家的通胀。

examples.en: The release shows changes in the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices for several groups of goods and services.
examples.zh: 这份发布材料列出了几类商品和服务的「调和消费者价格指数」变动情况。

collocations: publish the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices
Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices weights
changes in the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices

words.enDefinition: Selected purchase categories used together to represent spending in a price index

examples.en: The basket of goods and services in our example includes transport, rent and meals bought outside home.
examples.zh: 我们例子中的「商品和服务篮子」包含交通、房租和外出就餐。

examples.en: We priced the same basket of goods and services in two periods before calculating the index.
examples.zh: 计算指数前，我们先计算了两个时期同一「商品和服务篮子」的价格。

collocations: representative basket of goods and services
price a basket of goods and services
update the basket of goods and services

words.enDefinition: Share assigned to a category when calculating an overall index

examples.en: Rent has a larger index weight than fruit in the classroom's example price basket.
examples.zh: 在课堂示例的物价篮子里，房租的「指数权重」大于水果。

examples.en: We used the index weight and price movement to estimate the category's overall contribution.
examples.zh: 我们用「指数权重」和价格变动估算了该类别对总体变动的贡献。

words.enDefinition: Period whose index value serves as the reference for all readings

examples.en: We checked the index reference period before comparing the reported index levels across two tables.
examples.zh: 将两张表里列出的指数水平作比较前，我们先核对了「指数基准期」。

examples.en: The notes identify the index reference period as the year whose index value is one hundred.
examples.zh: 说明指出，「指数基准期」就是价格指数设定为一百的那一年。

words.enDefinition: a revision of the spending shares used as weights for categories in a consumer price index

examples.en: The expenditure weight update gave several household services a larger share because families' spending patterns had changed.
examples.zh: 由于家庭支出结构改变，「支出权重更新」提高了若干住户服务项目的权重。

examples.en: Our tutor compared the expenditure weight update with a change to the index's reference period.
examples.zh: 导师将「支出权重更新」与改变指数参考期的做法作了比较。

collocations: compare inflation before and after an expenditure weight update

words.enDefinition: Adjustment separating changes in a product's characteristics from changes in its price

examples.en: The index uses a quality adjustment after a laptop model is replaced by a faster version.
examples.zh: 笔记本电脑换成速度更快的型号后，该指数使用了「质量调整」。

examples.en: Our tutor explained quality adjustment using two refrigerators with different features and electricity use.
examples.zh: 老师用两款功能和耗电量不同的冰箱说明了「质量调整」。

words.enDefinition: Index distortion arising when weights miss shifts toward relatively cheaper purchases

examples.en: We discussed substitution bias after households switched from expensive pears to relatively cheaper apples.
examples.zh: 家庭消费者从较贵的梨转向相对便宜的苹果后，我们讨论了「替代偏差」。

examples.en: The fixed basket can create substitution bias when shoppers adjust what they purchase after prices change.
examples.zh: 价格变动后，购物者会调整所买商品，固定篮子可能因此产生「替代偏差」。

words.enDefinition: Estimated rental value of owner-occupied housing services in the US consumer index

examples.en: The US index uses owners' equivalent rent to track the cost of living in owned homes.
examples.zh: 美国的指数使用「业主等价租金」衡量住在自有住房里的成本。

examples.en: We compared owners' equivalent rent with actual tenant rents in the table's housing section.
examples.zh: 在统计表的住房部分，我们比较了「业主等价租金」和租户实际支付的租金。

words.enDefinition: Consumer price index adjusted to remove estimated recurring seasonal price movements

examples.en: We read the seasonally adjusted CPI to compare the index with the previous month.
examples.zh: 我们用「季调消费者价格指数」与前一个月作比较。

examples.en: In the table, the seasonally adjusted CPI rose less sharply than the unadjusted measure.
examples.zh: 统计表中的「季调消费者价格指数」涨幅小于未经调整的指标。

collocations: monthly change in seasonally adjusted CPI

words.enDefinition: Percentage change in the price index compared with the previous month

examples.en: Our chart uses month-over-month inflation to show how quickly prices changed from April to May.
examples.zh: 我们的图用「环比通胀」展示了四月到五月的价格变动速度。

examples.en: The month-over-month inflation figure rose while the twelve-month inflation rate fell in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在习题中，「环比通胀」读数上升，而十二个月通胀率下降。

words.enDefinition: Percentage change in the price index compared with the same month last year

examples.en: We computed year-over-year inflation for March using the previous March as our comparison month.
examples.zh: 我们使用上年三月为比较月份，计算了今年三月的「同比通胀」。

examples.en: The year-over-year inflation figure can fall as an especially large price rise leaves the comparison.
examples.zh: 此前一次特别大的价格上涨退出比较区间时，「同比通胀」读数可能下降。

words.enDefinition: Yearly equivalent implied by a shorter period's rate of price change

examples.en: We converted a quarterly price change to an annualized inflation rate for the class exercise.
examples.zh: 为完成课堂习题，我们把季度价格变化转换成了「年化通胀率」。

examples.en: The annualized inflation rate answers what yearly change the current monthly pace would imply.
examples.zh: 「年化通胀率」说明按当前每月变动速度推算，一年会变动多少。

words.enDefinition: Price growth measured across all categories covered by the selected index

examples.en: Higher energy prices lifted headline inflation in the exercise while other categories changed little.
examples.zh: 在习题中，能源价格上涨推高了「总体通胀」，而其他类别变化很小。

examples.en: We compared headline inflation across two reports based on different overall price indexes.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两份采用不同总体价格指数的报告里的「总体通胀」。

words.enDefinition: Measure of price growth designed to filter some volatile components

examples.en: The US example measures core inflation using a consumer index excluding food and energy.
examples.zh: 美国的这个例子用剔除食品和能源的消费价格指数衡量「核心通胀」。

examples.en: The professor explained why core inflation can differ depending on which series we use.
examples.zh: 老师解释了为什么选用的统计序列不同，「核心通胀」可能不同。

words.enDefinition: Rate of price increase for goods in the price measure

examples.en: Our chart shows goods inflation easing as prices of household equipment stop rising sharply.
examples.zh: 我们的图显示，家用设备价格停止急涨后，「商品通胀」有所缓和。

examples.en: The class compared goods inflation with changes in the prices of selected services.
examples.zh: 全班把「商品通胀」和部分服务价格的变动进行了比较。

words.enDefinition: Rate of price increase for services in the price measure

examples.en: We tracked services inflation separately to see how rents and restaurant prices changed.
examples.zh: 我们单独追踪「服务通胀」，以了解房租和餐厅价格如何变动。

examples.en: The briefing showed services inflation remaining positive even when prices for many goods fell.
examples.zh: 简报显示，即使许多商品的价格下跌，「服务通胀」仍为正。

words.enDefinition: Amount a component adds to or subtracts from overall price growth

examples.en: The report gives the inflation contribution of each category in percentage points.
examples.zh: 这份报告用百分点表示各类别的「通胀贡献」。

examples.en: We found a negative inflation contribution from fuel even though the overall index rose.
examples.zh: 虽然总体指数上涨，但燃油的「通胀贡献」为负。

words.enDefinition: Extent to which changes in inflation continue across periods after a disturbance

examples.en: The study found inflation persistence because inflation stayed elevated after the temporary shock faded.
examples.zh: 研究发现，尽管短期冲击消散，通胀仍居高不下，体现了「通胀持续性」。

examples.en: We compared inflation persistence in two model economies with different wage-setting arrangements.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两种工资设定方式不同的模型经济体的「通胀持续性」。

words.enDefinition: Price increases spread across many categories of household goods and services

examples.en: The report describes broad-based inflation after prices rose across most of the categories shown.
examples.zh: 报告显示，大多数类别的价格都上涨，出现了「广泛性通胀」。

examples.en: Our example distinguishes broad-based inflation from a temporary rise in just one category.
examples.zh: 我们的例子区分了「广泛性通胀」和仅有一个类别价格暂时上涨的情况。

words.enDefinition: Price growth driven by aggregate spending pressing against available productive capacity

examples.en: We modeled demand-pull inflation by increasing spending while keeping productive capacity unchanged.
examples.zh: 我们在产能不变的情况下增加支出，以模拟「需求拉动型通胀」。

examples.en: The example links demand-pull inflation to strong spending when factories are already busy.
examples.zh: 示例把工厂已经满负荷时的旺盛支出与「需求拉动型通胀」联系起来。

words.enDefinition: Price growth driven by higher production costs or adverse supply pressures

examples.en: We modeled cost-push inflation after higher energy costs made deliveries more expensive.
examples.zh: 能源成本上升使配送变贵后，我们对「成本推动型通胀」建模。

examples.en: The class discussed cost-push inflation using a temporary increase in the cost of imported materials.
examples.zh: 全班以进口原材料成本暂时增加为例讨论了「成本推动型通胀」。

words.enDefinition: Decline in a positive inflation rate while aggregate prices keep rising

examples.en: The chart shows disinflation when the annual price increase slows but stays positive.
examples.zh: 当年度价格涨幅放慢但仍为正时，图中显示的是「通胀放缓」。

examples.en: During disinflation, the price index in our example continued to move upward.
examples.zh: 在「通胀放缓」期间，例子中的价格指数仍继续上涨。

words.enDefinition: Combination of high inflation and weak or stagnant economic activity

examples.en: The model produced stagflation after a supply shock raised prices and lowered output.
examples.zh: 一次供给冲击使价格上升、产出下降后，模型出现了「滞胀」。

examples.en: We discussed stagflation when the case showed rising inflation alongside stagnant production.
examples.zh: 案例显示通胀加剧与生产停滞并存时，我们讨论了「滞胀」。

words.enDefinition: Extremely rapid and sustained increases in the general level of prices

examples.en: The historical case on hyperinflation shows how quickly the purchasing power of cash fell.
examples.zh: 关于「恶性通胀」的历史案例展示了现金购买力下降得有多快。

examples.en: The tutor used a monthly price chart to illustrate the scale of hyperinflation.
examples.zh: 老师用一张月度价格图来说明「恶性通胀」的幅度。

words.enDefinition: Wage measured by its purchasing power after adjustment for prices

examples.en: The real wage fell in our example because pay rose more slowly than prices.
examples.zh: 在我们的例子中，工资增速低于价格涨幅，因此「实际工资」下降了。

examples.en: We divided the money wage by a price index to estimate the real wage.
examples.zh: 我们将货币工资除以价格指数来估算「实际工资」。

words.enDefinition: Increase in pay over a specified period, usually expressed as a rate

examples.en: We compared wage growth with inflation to see whether pay gained purchasing power.
examples.zh: 我们将「工资增长」与通胀比较，判断工资购买力是否有所提高。

examples.en: The report compares wage growth across industries with different shares of part-time workers.
examples.zh: 这份报告比较了兼职人员占比不同的行业的「工资增长」。

words.enDefinition: labour compensation per unit of real output, under the source's coverage of output and labour

examples.en: The unit labor cost rose because hourly compensation increased more rapidly than output per hour.
examples.zh: 因为每小时劳动报酬上涨得比每小时产出快，「单位劳动成本」提高了。

examples.en: We divided total compensation by output to calculate unit labor cost in the example.
examples.zh: 在这个例子中，我们以总劳动报酬除以产量来计算「单位劳动成本」。

words.enDefinition: Feedback in which wage increases and price increases repeatedly reinforce each other

examples.en: The model shows a wage-price spiral when wages and prices keep pushing each other higher.
examples.zh: 工资和价格持续相互推升时，模型呈现出「工资价格螺旋」。

examples.en: We discussed whether a single pay increase was evidence of a wage-price spiral.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了一次加薪是否能成为「工资价格螺旋」的证据。

words.enDefinition: Adjusting amounts periodically in line with a specified measure of prices

examples.en: The model illustrates inflation indexation by linking payments to changes in a consumer index.
examples.zh: 模型把支付金额与消费价格指数的变化挂钩，说明「通胀指数化」。

examples.en: Our example compares fixed payments with another series that uses inflation indexation.
examples.zh: 这个例子将固定支付金额与采用「通胀指数化」的另一组金额作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Difference between inflation rates across economies, regions, or comparable groups

examples.en: We calculated the inflation differential between two regions using the same twelve-month comparison.
examples.zh: 我们采用相同的十二个月比较区间，计算两个地区的「通胀率之差」。

examples.en: The notes ask whether the inflation differential narrowed after energy prices stabilized in both regions.
examples.zh: 讲义问，在两地能源价格企稳后，「通胀率之差」是否缩小。

words.enDefinition: Model relationship between inflation or wage growth and labor market slack

examples.en: The lecturer introduced the Phillips curve using inflation and unemployment on separate axes.
examples.zh: 老师用分别标注通胀和失业的两条坐标轴介绍了「菲利普斯曲线」。

examples.en: We compared the Phillips curve across periods with different inflation expectations in the model.
examples.zh: 我们比较了模型中通胀预期不同的各个时期的「菲利普斯曲线」。

words.enDefinition: a model relation between inflation and unemployment or other slack measures with expectations and supply conditions held fixed

examples.en: We moved along the short-run Phillips curve while keeping expectations and supply conditions fixed.
examples.zh: 我们保持预期和供给条件不变，沿「短期菲利普斯曲线」移动。

examples.en: The diagram shifts the short-run Phillips curve upward after workers expect faster price increases.
examples.zh: 当劳动者预期价格上涨更快时，示意图中的「短期菲利普斯曲线」向上移动。

collocations: movement along the short-run Phillips curve

words.enDefinition: Vertical curve in the standard model after inflation expectations fully adjust

examples.en: In the textbook model, the long-run Phillips curve passes through the natural unemployment rate.
examples.zh: 在教科书模型中，「长期菲利普斯曲线」经过自然失业率所对应的位置。

examples.en: We drew a vertical long-run Phillips curve after allowing expectations to adjust fully in the model.
examples.zh: 允许模型中的预期充分调整后，我们画了一条垂直的「长期菲利普斯曲线」。

collocations: position of the long-run Phillips curve

words.zhGloss: 预期扩展的菲利普斯曲线
words.enDefinition: Model relating inflation to expected inflation, economic slack, and supply disturbances
acceptedZhAnswers: 预期扩展的菲利普斯曲线

examples.en: The expectations-augmented Phillips curve in our notes adds expected inflation to the basic model.
examples.zh: 我们笔记里的「预期扩展的菲利普斯曲线」在基本模型中加入了预期通胀。

examples.en: Our expectations-augmented Phillips curve exercise separates expected inflation from the effect of a temporary supply shock.
examples.zh: 关于「预期扩展的菲利普斯曲线」的习题将预期通胀和短期供给冲击的影响分开了。

words.enDefinition: Responsiveness of modeled inflation to a specified change in unemployment or slack

examples.en: We compared the Phillips curve slope in two models using the same unemployment measure.
examples.zh: 我们用相同的失业指标比较了两个模型中的「菲利普斯曲线斜率」。

examples.en: The smaller magnitude of the Phillips curve slope implies a weaker inflation response in our diagram.
examples.zh: 在我们的图中，「菲利普斯曲线斜率」的绝对值越小，意味着通胀对失业变动的反应越弱。

collocations: change in the Phillips curve slope

words.enDefinition: Model outcome where reducing inflation can temporarily require more unemployment

examples.en: Our model illustrates an inflation-unemployment trade-off in the short run when price expectations remain fixed.
examples.zh: 我们的模型说明了预期物价不变时短期内「通胀与失业的权衡」。

examples.en: The lecture asks how shifting expectations change the apparent inflation-unemployment trade-off over time.
examples.zh: 课堂讨论了预期变化如何改变不同时间观察到的「通胀与失业的权衡」。

words.enDefinition: Unemployment rate consistent with normal labor adjustment absent cyclical demand weakness

examples.en: Faster job matching lowered the natural rate of unemployment in the model used for class.
examples.zh: 在课堂所用的模型中，岗位匹配加快降低了「自然失业率」。

examples.en: We compared observed unemployment with an estimate of the natural rate of unemployment in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在习题中，我们把观测到的失业率和估计的「自然失业率」作了比较。

collocations: estimate the natural rate of unemployment
changes in the natural rate of unemployment
model the natural rate of unemployment

words.enDefinition: Unemployment rate at which inflation neither accelerates nor slows within a model

examples.en: The class estimated the NAIRU from a model relating unemployment to changes in inflation.
examples.zh: 全班利用一个把失业与通胀变化联系起来的模型，估算「非加速通胀失业率」。

examples.en: Two different sets of assumptions produced different estimates of the NAIRU in our exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，两套不同假设得出了不同的「非加速通胀失业率」估值。

words.enDefinition: Difference between observed unemployment and a benchmark such as its natural rate

examples.en: We calculated the unemployment gap by subtracting the benchmark rate from measured unemployment.
examples.zh: 我们用所测失业率减去基准失业率，求得「失业率缺口」。

examples.en: The model shows a positive unemployment gap when unemployment is above its estimated natural rate.
examples.zh: 模型显示，失业率高于估计的自然失业率时，「失业率缺口」为正。

words.enDefinition: Lasting effects of a temporary increase in unemployment on future joblessness

examples.en: The model links unemployment hysteresis to skills lost during prolonged periods without work.
examples.zh: 模型将「失业迟滞」与长时间无工作导致的技能流失联系起来。

examples.en: We discussed unemployment hysteresis after employment recovered more slowly than spending in the example.
examples.zh: 例子中的就业恢复慢于支出恢复，我们随后讨论了「失业迟滞」。

words.enDefinition: Beliefs about the likely rate of price increases over future periods

examples.en: The report compares inflation expectations among households and professional forecasters using the same time horizon.
examples.zh: 报告用同一个时间范围比较家庭和专业预测人士的「通胀预期」。

examples.en: The class discussed how inflation expectations can influence decisions about wages and prices today.
examples.zh: 课堂讨论了「通胀预期」会怎样影响当前的工资和定价决策。

words.enDefinition: Forecasts updated in response to past outcomes and previous forecast errors

examples.en: Our model uses adaptive expectations to revise next year's forecast after recent prices rise faster.
examples.zh: 我们的模型使用「适应性预期」，在近期价格上涨加快后修正明年的预测。

examples.en: We compared adaptive expectations with expectations based partly on announced policy changes in class.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂中比较了「适应性预期」和部分依据已公布的政策变化形成的预期。

words.enDefinition: Forecasts using available information consistently with the model, without systematic forecast errors

examples.en: We assumed rational expectations while allowing unexpected supply shocks to cause individual forecast errors.
examples.zh: 我们假定「理性预期」成立，同时允许意外的供给冲击造成个别预测误差。

examples.en: Under rational expectations, the model's forecast incorporates the policy announcement when it becomes known.
examples.zh: 在「理性预期」下，公众了解政策公告后，模型预测会把相关政策考虑进去。

words.enDefinition: Longer-term inflation beliefs remaining stable near a benchmark despite short-term changes

examples.en: The report describes anchored inflation expectations even though fuel prices raised this month's inflation reading.
examples.zh: 报告称，尽管燃油推高了本月通胀读数，仍可观察到「锚定的通胀预期」。

examples.en: The survey's ten-year projection stayed near the target, illustrating anchored inflation expectations in our example.
examples.zh: 在我们的例子中，调查所得的十年期预测仍接近目标，体现了「锚定的通胀预期」。

words.enDefinition: Loss of a stable anchor for longer-term expectations about price changes

examples.en: We discussed possible de-anchoring of inflation expectations after long-term survey forecasts moved away from the target.
examples.zh: 长期调查预测偏离目标后，我们讨论了「通胀预期脱锚」的可能性。

examples.en: The case study illustrates de-anchoring of inflation expectations after a series of unexpected price increases.
examples.zh: 案例展示了一连串意外涨价后出现的「通胀预期脱锚」。

collocations: risk of de-anchoring of inflation expectations
evidence of de-anchoring of inflation expectations

words.enDefinition: Difference between realized inflation and the rate previously expected for that period

examples.en: The plot shows a positive inflation surprise when observed inflation exceeds the previous forecast.
examples.zh: 实际通胀高于先前预测时，图上显示为正向「通胀意外」。

examples.en: We measured the inflation surprise by comparing the reading with the survey estimate from June.
examples.zh: 我们把实际读数与六月调查估值作比较，衡量了「通胀意外」。

words.enDefinition: Cumulative output loss associated with lowering inflation by one percentage point

examples.en: We estimated the sacrifice ratio from lost output during a modeled decline in inflation.
examples.zh: 我们根据模型中通胀下降期间的产出损失估算了「牺牲率」。

examples.en: The lecture compared the sacrifice ratio under two assumptions about how quickly expectations adjust.
examples.zh: 课堂在两种不同的预期调整速度假设下，比较了「牺牲率」。

words.enDefinition: Tendency of wages measured in money to adjust slowly, especially downward

examples.en: The model assumes nominal wage rigidity because existing hourly contracts reset only once a year.
examples.zh: 现有的计时工资合同每年只调整一次，因此模型假定存在「名义工资刚性」。

examples.en: We compared nominal wage rigidity with a model where wages immediately respond to demand changes.
examples.zh: 我们把「名义工资刚性」与工资立即响应需求变化的模型作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Stock of money available under the specific aggregate definition being used

examples.en: The lecture compares two measures of the money supply that include different deposits.
examples.zh: 课堂比较了两种纳入不同存款类别的「货币供给量」指标。

examples.en: We examined how the reported money supply changed after a shift between account types.
examples.zh: 我们研究了存款在账户类型之间转移后，公布的「货币供给量」如何变化。

words.enDefinition: Amount of spendable balances people wish to hold under given conditions

examples.en: The model shows greater demand for money when households make more purchases each week.
examples.zh: 这个模型显示，家庭每周购买活动增加时「货币需求」变大。

examples.en: We compared the demand for money at two interest rates while holding income fixed.
examples.zh: 我们保持收入不变，比较了两种利率下的「货币需求」。

collocations: increase in the demand for money

words.enDefinition: Preference for holding easily spendable balances instead of less liquid assets

examples.en: The example links stronger liquidity preference to greater uncertainty about upcoming household expenses.
examples.zh: 例子把更强的「流动性偏好」与未来家庭开支的不确定性增大联系起来。

examples.en: We used liquidity preference theory to explain the model's downward-sloping demand for money.
examples.zh: 我们用「流动性偏好」理论解释模型中向下倾斜的货币需求曲线。

words.enDefinition: Textbook condition where desired money holdings equal the amount supplied

examples.en: Our model reaches money market equilibrium where the supply of money equals desired holdings.
examples.zh: 在我们的模型中，货币供给量等于所需持有量时达到「货币市场均衡」。

examples.en: We redrew the money market equilibrium diagram after changing the assumed level of income.
examples.zh: 修改收入水平假设后，我们重新画了「货币市场均衡」图。

words.enDefinition: Statistical measure grouping together specified types of money and liquid balances

examples.en: The lecture explains why the monetary aggregate includes some accounts and excludes others.
examples.zh: 课堂解释了「货币总量指标」为什么纳入某些账户而排除其他账户。

examples.en: We chose the same monetary aggregate before comparing money growth across the two periods.
examples.zh: 比较两个时期的货币增长之前，我们选定了同一个「货币总量指标」。

words.enDefinition: Money measure emphasizing currency and balances available for relatively immediate spending

examples.en: The report describes narrow money as the more readily spendable portion of the measure.
examples.zh: 报告将「狭义货币」称为该指标中较容易直接用于支出的部分。

examples.en: Our cross-country table defines narrow money separately for each economy in the comparison.
examples.zh: 我们的跨国统计表分别给出参与比较的各经济体对「狭义货币」的定义。

words.enDefinition: Money measure including additional liquid assets beyond the narrower transaction balances

examples.en: The definition of broad money in this report includes some extra categories of deposits.
examples.zh: 这份报告对「广义货币」的定义包含一些额外的存款类别。

examples.en: We compared broad money growth only after checking what the two reports included.
examples.zh: 我们先核对两份报告的统计范围，再比较「广义货币」的增长情况。

words.enDefinition: Measure combining currency in circulation with banks' reserves at the central bank

examples.en: Our table gives the monetary base separately from the broader measures that include customer deposits.
examples.zh: 我们的统计表把「基础货币」与包括客户存款的较广义指标分开列出。

examples.en: An increase in bank reserves raised the monetary base in the classroom accounting example.
examples.zh: 在课堂的会计示例中，银行准备金增加使「基础货币」增加。

words.enDefinition: notes and coins issued and held outside the institutions excluded by the monetary statistic's stated definition

examples.en: Our data table separates currency in circulation from reserve balances held at the central bank.
examples.zh: 我们的数据表把「流通中货币」和央行持有的银行准备金余额分开列出。

examples.en: We checked whether the definition of currency in circulation in this series included cash held by banks.
examples.zh: 我们核查这个统计序列对「流通中货币」的定义是否包括银行持有的现金。

words.enDefinition: assets banks hold as reserves, including balances at their central bank and sometimes vault cash depending on the reporting definition

examples.en: The model shows how payments between lenders are settled using bank reserves at the central bank.
examples.zh: 模型展示了贷款机构之间如何利用央行账户中的「银行准备金」进行结算。

examples.en: Our worksheet compares bank reserves with the deposits that households hold at commercial banks.
examples.zh: 习题比较了「银行准备金」和家庭在商业银行持有的存款。

words.enDefinition: Rule specifying reserves banks must maintain against certain liabilities under a framework

examples.en: The textbook model assumes a reserve requirement tied to a specified group of deposits.
examples.zh: 教材模型假定「法定准备金要求」与指定类别的存款有关。

examples.en: We compared two banking frameworks with different ways of setting the reserve requirement.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两种以不同方式设定「法定准备金要求」的银行制度。

words.enDefinition: Ratio of a chosen money stock to the monetary base

examples.en: The worksheet compares the money multiplier under different assumptions about cash and excess reserves.
examples.zh: 习题比较了对现金及超额准备金作出不同假设时的「货币乘数」。

examples.en: In this example, the money multiplier is smaller because households hold more cash.
examples.zh: 在这个例子中，家庭持有更多现金，所以「货币乘数」更小。

words.enDefinition: Interest rate a central bank sets or targets to implement policy

examples.en: Our model raises the policy rate before tracing what happens to borrowing and spending.
examples.zh: 我们的模型先提高「政策利率」，再追踪借款和支出的变化。

examples.en: The statement explained why the committee held the policy rate steady in the scenario.
examples.zh: 这份声明解释了在该情景下委员会为何维持「政策利率」不变。

words.enDefinition: Rate on unsecured overnight loans in the US federal funds market

examples.en: We plotted the federal funds rate to compare it with the target range in the example.
examples.zh: 我们绘制了「联邦基金利率」，将它与示例中的目标区间作比较。

examples.en: The notes connect the federal funds rate to overnight lending among eligible US financial institutions.
examples.zh: 讲义将「联邦基金利率」与符合条件的美国金融机构之间的隔夜拆借联系起来。

collocations: target range for the federal funds rate

words.enDefinition: Interest the US Federal Reserve pays eligible institutions on their reserve balances

examples.en: Our notes explain why interest on reserve balances matters when banks compare the returns on overnight assets.
examples.zh: 讲义解释了为什么银行比较隔夜资产收益时会关注「准备金余额利息」。

examples.en: The US example shows how interest on reserve balances helps guide overnight interest rates toward the target range.
examples.zh: 美国例子展示了「准备金余额利息」如何帮助引导隔夜利率向目标区间靠近。

collocations: rate of interest on reserve balances

words.enDefinition: US Federal Reserve committee responsible for monetary policy decisions including rate targets

examples.en: We read the Federal Open Market Committee statement to identify the arguments for holding rates steady.
examples.zh: 我们阅读「联邦公开市场委员会」的声明，找出维持利率不变的理由。

examples.en: The lesson compares a Federal Open Market Committee decision with the market's earlier expectations for rates.
examples.zh: 课堂将「联邦公开市场委员会」的一项决定与市场先前的利率预期作了比较。

words.enDefinition: US policy goals of maximum employment and stable prices, considered together

examples.en: The Fed case uses the dual mandate to discuss employment alongside inflation.
examples.zh: 关于美联储的案例用「双重使命」说明为何把就业和通胀一同考虑。

examples.en: We compared decisions under a dual mandate with those under a price stability objective alone.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「双重使命」下的决策和只有物价稳定这一目标时的决策。

words.enDefinition: Condition of low and sufficiently stable inflation over the relevant horizon

examples.en: Our example treats price stability as compatible with small movements in relative prices.
examples.zh: 我们的例子认为，「物价稳定」与相对价格的小幅变动可以并存。

examples.en: The lesson explains why the central bank's measure of price stability covers many prices.
examples.zh: 课堂解释了为什么央行衡量「物价稳定」的指标涵盖许多价格。

words.enDefinition: Specified inflation rate or range a central bank seeks over time

examples.en: We compared the inflation target with the expected inflation rate over the same horizon.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「通胀目标」和相同时段内的预期通胀率。

examples.en: The case study examines how policymakers explain a temporary deviation from the inflation target.
examples.zh: 案例研究了政策制定者如何解释暂时偏离「通胀目标」。

words.enDefinition: Framework using a stated inflation objective to guide and explain monetary policy

examples.en: The course used inflation targeting to discuss why some central banks publish inflation forecasts.
examples.zh: 课堂以「通胀目标制」为例，讨论一些央行为什么公布通胀预测。

examples.en: Our model illustrates inflation targeting when the central bank responds to forecasts of above-target inflation.
examples.zh: 当央行对高于目标的通胀预测作出反应时，我们的模型展示了「通胀目标制」。

words.enDefinition: Central bank market transactions used to manage reserves or implement policy

examples.en: The textbook illustrates open market operations with a central bank purchase of government securities.
examples.zh: 教材用央行购买政府证券的例子说明「公开市场操作」。

examples.en: Our class compared open market operations with borrowing directly from the central bank's lending facility.
examples.zh: 全班把「公开市场操作」与直接通过央行贷款工具借款作了比较。

words.enDefinition: US Federal Reserve lending facility for eligible institutions posting acceptable collateral

examples.en: The US banking example uses the discount window to illustrate short-term central bank lending.
examples.zh: 美国银行业案例通过「贴现窗口」展示了央行短期放贷。

examples.en: Our reading compares the discount window with borrowing at a market interest rate.
examples.zh: 阅读材料将「贴现窗口」与按市场利率借款作了比较。

words.enDefinition: System using administered rates when reserve balances are sufficiently abundant

examples.en: The report explains how administered rates guide markets under the ample reserves framework.
examples.zh: 报告解释了在「充足准备金框架」下，管理利率如何引导市场。

examples.en: We compared the ample reserves framework with a system using routinely scarce reserve balances.
examples.zh: 我们将「充足准备金框架」和一种日常准备金供应偏紧的制度作了比较。

collocations: operate with an ample reserves framework
implement policy under an ample reserves framework

words.enDefinition: Level near which additional policy rate cuts become impractical or ineffective

examples.en: The model reaches the effective lower bound before exploring other ways to loosen monetary policy.
examples.zh: 模型先达到「有效利率下限」，再探讨其他放松货币政策的方式。

examples.en: We discussed why estimates of the effective lower bound can differ across banking systems.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么不同银行体系对「有效利率下限」的估计会不同。

collocations: policy at the effective lower bound

words.enDefinition: Central bank communication about likely future policy or conditions guiding decisions

examples.en: The committee used forward guidance to explain what data could justify another rate change.
examples.zh: 委员会通过「前瞻指引」说明哪些数据可能支持再次调整利率。

examples.en: Our class analyzed how forward guidance might affect expected short-term rates before policy changes.
examples.zh: 全班分析了政策改变前「前瞻指引」可能如何影响预期短期利率。

words.enDefinition: Large-scale central bank asset purchases intended to ease broader financial conditions

examples.en: We studied quantitative easing as a policy option when short-term rates were already low.
examples.zh: 我们把「量化宽松」作为短期利率已经很低时的一种政策选项来研究。

examples.en: The model examines how quantitative easing could affect long-term yields through asset purchases.
examples.zh: 模型研究了「量化宽松」如何通过购买资产影响长期收益率。

words.enDefinition: Reduction in a central bank's asset holdings through maturities or sales

examples.en: The case illustrates quantitative tightening by letting some government bonds mature without replacing them.
examples.zh: 案例用部分政府债券到期后不再补购的做法来说明「量化紧缩」。

examples.en: Our discussion covers how quantitative tightening may affect reserves as the central bank's portfolio shrinks.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了央行持有的资产规模收缩时，「量化紧缩」可能如何影响准备金。

words.enDefinition: Reduction in holdings as maturing assets are allowed to roll off

examples.en: The central bank model shows balance sheet runoff when some maturing bonds are not replaced.
examples.zh: 在央行模型中，部分到期债券未获补购，出现了「资产自然到期缩表」。

examples.en: We compared gradual balance sheet runoff with an alternative involving outright sales of existing bonds.
examples.zh: 我们将逐步「资产自然到期缩表」与直接卖出现有债券的方案作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Process through which policy decisions affect financial conditions, activity, and inflation

examples.en: We drew a diagram of monetary policy transmission starting with a rise in policy rates.
examples.zh: 我们绘制了以政策利率上调开始的「货币政策传导」图。

examples.en: The article explains why monetary policy transmission can be faster in some credit markets.
examples.zh: 文章解释了为什么「货币政策传导」在某些信贷市场可能更快。

words.enDefinition: Transmission of monetary policy through changes in borrowing costs and spending

examples.en: Our example traces the interest rate channel from a rate cut to lower loan costs.
examples.zh: 示例展示了「利率渠道」如何把降息传导为较低的贷款成本。

examples.en: We distinguished the interest rate channel from effects caused by banks changing credit standards.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「利率渠道」和银行调整信贷标准产生的影响。

collocations: effects of the interest rate channel

words.enDefinition: Policy transmission through changes in banks' ability or willingness to lend

examples.en: The lecture links the bank lending channel to changes in loan supply after policy tightening.
examples.zh: 课堂把「银行信贷渠道」与政策收紧后贷款供给的变化联系起来。

examples.en: The case study compares the bank lending channel across banks facing different funding conditions.
examples.zh: 案例研究比较了面对不同融资条件的银行所体现的「银行信贷渠道」。

collocations: strength of the bank lending channel

words.enDefinition: Characterization of policy as stimulating, neutral, or restraining economic activity

examples.en: We used estimated real interest rates to discuss the model's monetary policy stance.
examples.zh: 我们用估计的实际利率讨论模型中的货币「政策立场」。

examples.en: The report calls the policy stance restrictive even after a small reduction in rates.
examples.zh: 尽管利率已小幅下调，报告仍将「政策立场」称为限制性的。

words.enDefinition: Shift toward a policy stance intended to support spending and borrowing

examples.en: The textbook scenario uses monetary easing to illustrate a possible response to weaker demand.
examples.zh: 教材情景用「货币政策宽松」举例说明需求转弱时的一种可能应对方式。

examples.en: We compared the effects of monetary easing after fast and slow changes in lending rates.
examples.zh: 我们比较了贷款利率快速和缓慢调整时「货币政策宽松」的效果。

words.enDefinition: Shift toward a more restrictive policy stance intended to restrain demand

examples.en: The model traces monetary tightening from higher policy rates to softer demand for credit.
examples.zh: 模型追踪了「货币政策收紧」如何从政策利率上涨传导到信贷需求转弱。

examples.en: Our exercise asks why monetary tightening may influence inflation only after a delay.
examples.zh: 习题问，为什么「货币政策收紧」可能要过一段时间才影响通胀。

words.enDefinition: Interest rate adjusted for either observed or expected inflation

examples.en: We approximated the real interest rate by subtracting expected inflation from the nominal rate.
examples.zh: 我们从名义利率中减去预期通胀率，估算了「实际利率」。

examples.en: In our example, the real interest rate rose even though the quoted rate stayed fixed.
examples.zh: 在我们的例子里，尽管公布的利率保持不变，「实际利率」仍上升了。

words.enDefinition: an estimated interest rate consistent with output at potential and stable inflation over the relevant horizon

examples.en: Our model uses a neutral interest rate to judge whether the policy rate restrains activity.
examples.zh: 模型用「中性利率」来判断政策利率是否抑制经济活动。

examples.en: The reading discusses why the neutral interest rate must be inferred instead of observed directly.
examples.zh: 阅读材料讨论了为什么「中性利率」需要推断，无法直接观测。

collocations: uncertainty around the neutral interest rate

words.enDefinition: Illustrative formula linking a policy rate to inflation and economic activity gaps

examples.en: We used a Taylor rule to compare rate prescriptions under two inflation forecasts.
examples.zh: 我们用「泰勒规则」比较了两种通胀预测下公式所指示的利率。

examples.en: The lecture changes a Taylor rule coefficient to show a larger response to inflation.
examples.zh: 课堂调整「泰勒规则」中的一个系数，展示对通胀反应更强的情形。

words.enDefinition: Policy aimed at limiting large fluctuations in activity, employment, or inflation

examples.en: Our class compared two approaches to stabilization policy after demand fell in the model.
examples.zh: 总需求在模型中下降后，全班比较了两种「稳定政策」的做法。

examples.en: The chapter discusses stabilization policy when inflation rises even as employment falls in the model.
examples.zh: 该章节讨论了模型中就业下滑而通胀上升时的「稳定政策」。

words.enDefinition: Existing tax or spending feature damping fluctuations without a new policy decision

examples.en: The textbook treats income tax as an automatic stabilizer when earnings fall during downturns.
examples.zh: 教材将经济下行中收入下降时的所得税视为「自动稳定器」。

examples.en: Our simplified model includes an automatic stabilizer that raises benefit payments when unemployment rises.
examples.zh: 我们的简化模型有一个「自动稳定器」，它会在失业上升时增加福利支付。

words.enDefinition: Deliberate changes in taxation or public spending through new policy decisions

examples.en: The lecture illustrates discretionary fiscal policy with a newly approved increase in public spending.
examples.zh: 课堂中新批准的公共支出增长是「主动财政政策」的一个例子。

examples.en: We contrasted discretionary fiscal policy with tax revenues changing automatically when household incomes fall.
examples.zh: 我们把「主动财政政策」与家庭收入下降时税收自动变化的情形作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Tax or spending change intended to increase aggregate spending or activity

examples.en: The model illustrates a fiscal expansion by raising government purchases during weak private spending.
examples.zh: 这个模型展示了私人支出疲弱时增加政府购买支出的「财政扩张」。

examples.en: We compared a tax-based fiscal expansion with a change in government purchases in class.
examples.zh: 全班比较了以税收调整为手段的「财政扩张」和政府购买支出的变化。

words.enDefinition: Tax or spending change intended to reduce aggregate spending or activity

examples.en: Our worksheet models a fiscal contraction by reducing public spending when private demand is strong.
examples.zh: 习题用私人需求旺盛时削减公共支出的方法来模拟「财政紧缩」。

examples.en: We discussed the possible effects of a fiscal contraction before changing any other model assumptions.
examples.zh: 调整其他模型假设前，我们讨论了「财政紧缩」可能带来的影响。

words.enDefinition: Delay before policymakers recognize a change in the state of the economy

examples.en: The model includes a recognition lag because economic statistics arrive after conditions change.
examples.zh: 模型有「识别时滞」，因为经济形势变化后，相关统计数据才会发布。

examples.en: The class discussed the recognition lag when later revisions revealed an earlier downturn.
examples.zh: 后续修订揭示了更早发生的经济下行，全班讨论了其中的「识别时滞」。

words.enDefinition: Delay between deciding on a policy and putting it into effect

examples.en: The project example illustrates an implementation lag between approval and actual construction spending.
examples.zh: 该项目示例说明了批准与实际发生建设支出之间的「实施时滞」。

examples.en: Our chart places the implementation lag after the government chooses a fiscal measure.
examples.zh: 我们的图把「实施时滞」放在政府选定财政措施之后。

words.enDefinition: Time after policy implementation before its economic effects become evident

examples.en: We modeled an impact lag between a change in rates and changes in household spending.
examples.zh: 我们模拟了利率变动与家庭支出变化之间的「作用时滞」。

examples.en: The lecture uses the impact lag to explain why inflation may respond gradually.
examples.zh: 课堂用「作用时滞」解释了为什么通胀可能逐步作出反应。

words.enDefinition: Tax and spending choices that amplify expansions or downturns in aggregate activity

examples.en: The worksheet illustrates procyclical fiscal policy by reducing public spending when private demand already falls.
examples.zh: 习题以私人需求已经下滑时削减公共支出为例说明「顺周期财政政策」。

examples.en: We compared procyclical fiscal policy with a response designed to cushion the modeled downturn.
examples.zh: 我们将「顺周期财政政策」与旨在缓冲模型中经济下行的政策反应作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Tax and spending choices that offset expansions or downturns in aggregate activity

examples.en: The lecture models countercyclical fiscal policy by raising purchases after a drop in private spending.
examples.zh: 课堂通过在私人支出下降后提高政府购买，来模拟「逆周期财政政策」。

examples.en: We compared two examples of countercyclical fiscal policy that used different mixes of taxes and spending.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个采用不同税收和支出组合的「逆周期财政政策」示例。

words.zhGloss: 周期调整后的预算余额
words.enDefinition: Estimated budget balance after removing the temporary effects of economic fluctuations
acceptedZhAnswers: 周期调整后的预算余额

examples.en: The example uses a cyclically adjusted budget balance to separate weak tax receipts from other budget changes.
examples.zh: 该例使用「周期调整后的预算余额」，将税收收入因经济疲弱而减少的影响与其他预算变化分离。

examples.en: Our estimate of the cyclically adjusted budget balance changes when we revise assumed potential output.
examples.zh: 调整假定的潜在产出之后，我们对「周期调整后的预算余额」的估值也发生了变化。

collocations: calculate the cyclically adjusted budget balance
improve the cyclically adjusted budget balance

words.enDefinition: Reduction in private spending associated with an increase in government borrowing or expenditure

examples.en: Our model illustrates crowding out when higher government borrowing raises rates and reduces private investment.
examples.zh: 我们的模型展示了政府借款增加导致利率上升、私人投资减少时的「挤出效应」。

examples.en: The exercise compares crowding out under two assumptions about how interest rates respond.
examples.zh: 习题在两种不同的利率反应假设下比较了「挤出效应」。
